7. IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE COMMITMENTS OF RESOURCES
7.1 LAND FEATURES AND USES
During the life of the proposed project, some present uses of the area would be preempted. However, all the land areas that would be used for the project could be restored to a state similar to the present conditions, if the project were removed and appropriate rehabilitative measures were undertaken. Present dispersed outdoor recreation opportunities within the proposed reservoir basin would be altered or lost for the life of the project through clearing and subsequent inundation of the existing land and water features.
7.2 ENDANGERED SPECIES AND ECOSYSTEMS
7.2.1 Flora
The rare and uncommon plant species discussed in Subsection 2.2.3 could be irretrievably lost from the project area as a result of the proposed action. Even if all project facilities were removed and the endemic vegetation of the area reestablished, the rare forms might never return because the correct environmental conditions might never reoccur. Many environmental variables could adversely affect the reestablishment of these rare plant species.
7.2.2 Fauna
Wildlife populations dependent on the type of habitat to be eliminated by the project would be forced to either immigrate to adjacent areas of suitable habitat or die. If these adjacent areas are at their carrying capacity, the numbers of wildlife in excess of that level could be lost.
Such endangered species as the southern bald eagle and the American peregrine falcon, as described in Subsection 2.2.3, could possibly by affected by the proposed project. Neither of these birds have been sighted in the proposed project area. The Bad Creek area lies within the former range of the resident race of the peregrine falcon and, should an attempt be made to reestablish the species to areas of its former breeding range (see Subsection 2.2.3), loss of the area occupied by the proposed project would limit the habitat accordingly.
